title: Tiling ribbon: Floor ticket
topics: Greedy choices, dynamic programming and backtracking
summary: For each width x, count the ordered ways to fill a one-row ribbon using pieces of widths 1 and 3. A width of 0 has one empty arrangement. Produce the counts in input order. Return the smallest value in the derived sequence, or 0 for an empty sequence.
descriptionMd:
The display desk builds narrow paper ribbons from one-unit and three-unit printed pieces. Neri is checking the lower stop before the ribbon press opens. A negative reading is a real measurement and must not be replaced by an invented zero.

For each width x, count the ordered ways to fill a one-row ribbon using pieces of widths 1 and 3. A width of 0 has one empty arrangement. Produce the counts in input order.

Return the smallest value in the derived sequence, or 0 for an empty sequence.

Implement tilingRibbonFloorTicket(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Counting dynamic programming. For each width x, count the ordered ways to fill a one-row ribbon using pieces of widths 1 and 3. A width of 0 has one empty arrangement. Produce the counts in input order. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.

Target time O(n + M); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with counting dynamic programming. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

For each width x, count the ordered ways to fill a one-row ribbon using pieces of widths 1 and 3. A width of 0 has one empty arrangement. Produce the counts in input order. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return the smallest value in the derived sequence, or 0 for an empty sequence. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.
